fields.dct:description: The rate of increase in mean fitness of a population due to natural selection equals its additive genetic variance in fitness at that time.
fields.dct:source: Ronald A. Fisher (1930) The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection
fields.delphi:context: Assumptions: the 'partial change' holds average effects of alleles and the environment fixed (Price 1972, Ewens 1989); V_A is the additive genetic variance in fitness. Formal status: proved in this partial-change reading. Read as a claim about the total change in mean fitness it is false under dominance, epistasis, frequency dependence or a changing environment.
fields.delphi:proposedTest: In a pedigreed wild population or an experimental-evolution line, estimate the additive genetic variance in relative fitness (animal model) and compare it with the observed per-generation response of breeding values for fitness, separating the selection term from environmental deterioration.
fields.rdfs:label: Fisher's fundamental theorem of natural selection (partial-change form)
fields.skos:notation: \Delta_{NS}\bar{w} = V_A(w)/\bar{w} (discrete generations); \left.\frac{d\bar{m}}{dt}\right|_{NS} = V_A(m) for Malthusian fitness m
